findings.why: Composed-screen contradiction. The monitors header reads «{count} فعال» (armed) and dormant rows are counted in it (monitorAlerting excludes dormant, so the header stays «5 فعال»), while the dormant row's own slot says «غیر فعال» — the literal antonym of فعال — directly beneath. It also spends the standard Urdu word for DISABLED (core uses غیر فعال for disabled) on the weaker state while the stronger state, disabled, is «بند». Rendered: header «5 فعال» + dormant slot «غیر فعال» (before) vs «خوابیدہ» (after). If خوابیدہ is judged too literary: «سویا ہوا». Not «معطل» (collides with the parked clause's meaning).
findings.verified: tsx repl.ts 'S1 composed BEFORE/AFTER' lines in audit.log; read of schedules-copy.ts monitorAlerting/monitorSectionSummary; core ur grep for غیر فعال=disabled (wire.errors.desktop.aida_disabled).

findings.why: Glossary inconsistency on one screen. The three supervisor sentences are alternatives of one status line: unsupported/unverifiable say «بیداریوں کی نگرانی» for 'supervised', only not_running introduces a transliterated «سپروائزر». i18n/glossary.md note 7 records, for ur, that 'supervised' is rendered with the existing monitor word نگرانی because none of the locales has a settled word for a supervisor unit and inventing one would give one concept two names; core tui.schedule.notice_supervisor does the same. Replacement keeps that call, names the thing descriptively, and agrees in gender (سروس is feminine: چل نہیں رہی).
findings.verified: git show origin/main:i18n/glossary.md note 7; core tui.schedule.notice_supervisor; replacement parsed and rendered via parseMessage/formatMessage in repl.ts.
